title: Protocol adapter examples: compact polyglot streaming & tool schemas
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a set of concrete protocol-adapter examples and lightweight reference implementations (TypeScript, Python, Go) that demonstrate: 1) a compact framing/envelope for progressive streaming + partial JSON tool-call payloads; 2) a compatibility adapter that maps legacy non-streaming client semantics to the new streaming contract; 3) structured-output validation points (schema-first + permissive parsing) for resource-constrained SDKs. The intent is to give integrators fast, copy-pasteable patterns for handling incremental tool invocations, resumable sessions, and schema-validated fragments without shipping a heavy runtime. This ticket produces code snippets, a migration guide, unit tests, and a short perf note comparing prefix-latency and token-throughput against the current reference SDK.

acceptance_criteria: Three reference adapters (TypeScript, Python, Go) implementing the compact framing protocol and tool-call envelope with example usages
Migration guide with step-by-step mapping from legacy call semantics to streaming + tool frames
Unit tests covering partial-frame parsing, schema-fallback behavior, and resumable session example
Bench report showing prefix-latency and tokens/sec for the compact envelope vs standard newline-delimited JSON stream
Example integration PR for one internal reference app (console-cli) that demonstrates resume + tool retry flow
implementation_notes: Framing: use 1-byte type + 4-byte big-endian length header for compactness and C-friendly parsing
Parser strategy: streaming-safe incremental JSON parser with permissive mode that emits 'fragment' events; finalization step validates against provided JSON Schema if present
Backcompat: provide adapter that buffers a single 'response' from fragments and exposes old promise-based API; also expose streaming iterator for new clients
Error handling: tool-call frames must include an id field; runtime will ack tool-start/tool-end frames to enable idempotent retries
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: embedded devices may still struggle with partial JSON reassembly. Mitigation: supply a line-delimited JSON alternative in examples and document trade-offs.
Risk: schema validation on finalization can be expensive. Mitigation: recommend lightweight schema-hints and optional server-side pre-validation for large corpora.
Risk: concurrency semantics between KV cache updates and tool results. Mitigation: add explicit sync frame and document ordering guarantees.
Risk: developer confusion with multiple framing formats. Mitigation: include a clear decision table in the migration guide and a 'choose your adapter' quick start.
Risk: potential telemetry gap for early adopters. Mitigation: include example OTEL spans in TS/py adapters and a minimal Prometheus metric export for Go.
